overall: The AG found neither the School Committee nor its Community Relations Subcommittee violated the Open Meeting Law; the resume review never became a meeting or deliberation, and no remedy was ordered.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the two-member Community Relations Subcommittee deliberated outside a noticed meeting by reviewing applicant resumes for a Community Relations Specialist.
allegations.key_passage: Ms. Sovinee and Dr. Brown spoke outside of a meeting only to attempt to schedule a Subcommittee meeting.

allegations.summary: Whether the subcommittee members' individual review of resumes and their discussion of them amounted to a meeting or deliberation outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Additionally, we find that the Subcommittee never met and Ms. Sovinee and Dr. Brown did not otherwise discuss the resumes with each other.

allegations.summary: Whether the two members' attendance at an October 2013 communications training, which the chair's colleague described as a Subcommittee meeting, required posted notice.
allegations.key_passage: Ms. Sovinee and Dr. Brown attended this event before the Subcommittee was created, thus there was no need for them to post notice of a Subcommittee meeting on that date.

allegations.summary: Whether one subcommittee member's participation in candidate interviews with the superintendent constituted an unposted deliberation.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
